files.why: Add a runtime query (e.g. fetchRescheduleEnabled(customerId)) so the on/off state is read from the server per request — the 'without deploying' requirement means it must be fetched, not compiled in.
Add the server-shape (snake_case) Zod schema for the per-customer flag response the new query parses; DTOs must live in data/.
Map the flag DTO to the plain core shape the UI consumes, keeping the snake_case wire format from leaking above data/.
Add an MSW handler for the flag endpoint so the flag is toggleable in dev/tests and the two states (on/off) can actually be exercised.

New composable that reactively loads and exposes whether reschedule is enabled for the current customer; feature-rollout is a different reason-to-change than day-schedule loading (rule 6), so it is its own composable rather than folded into useDaySchedule.
Gate the 'Reschedule' button and inline RescheduleForm on the flag so the flow disappears when the customer has it turned off.
Defense-in-depth: refuse submit() when the flag is off so turning the flow 'off' also blocks the mutation, not just hides the button.

uncertain: Whether the gating belongs in core/policy.ts (fold a `featureEnabled` param into canReschedule/validateReschedule) instead of only the data+UI layers. I treated 'feature is turned on for this customer' as runtime availability config, not a domain invariant like the 24h rule, so I kept it out of framework-free core — but a case exists for making core the single decision point.

Whether mappers.ts is needed at all: if the endpoint returns a bare boolean, the query can return it directly and no mapper/DTO change is warranted. I included both to follow the DTO->core convention, but a trivial payload may make dto.ts/mappers.ts edits unnecessary.
Separate useRescheduleAvailability composable vs. extending useDaySchedule — both satisfy the boundary rules; I chose separation on reason-to-change grounds, but the team may prefer one fetch.

Placement in the scheduling slice vs. shared/. Per rule 7 (3+ same-reason usages before promotion) a single reschedule flag stays in-slice, but if a general per-customer feature-flag platform is intended this would instead be a new shared/http or shared/lib concern plus an app-level provider — a much larger change I did NOT assume.
questions: How is the 'current customer' identified at runtime? There is no auth/session/tenant concept anywhere in src today, and the flag query needs a customer id to read the flag for.

Does 'per customer' mean the tenant/account operating Vise, or the client whose appointment is being rescheduled (c-ana, c-ben in the seed)? The gating point differs (whole DayView vs. per-appointment).
Is there an existing feature-flag service/endpoint and payload contract to conform to, or do we define a new /api/... endpoint here (and is the server side in scope)?
What is the server-side toggle mechanism that flips the flag without a deploy (admin UI, config service)? This ticket only covers the frontend read/gate; confirm the backend toggle exists.
Should the flag also stop appointments mid-flow (e.g. hide/disable an already-open RescheduleForm) or only affect new entries into the flow?
